title.title: The Writing of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

lg.l: From dark dull woods emerging into day
We pass where farms their opening fields display
Barns, fences, cottages, lawns appeared.
Where various sounds of human toil were heard we hear
There around a hut upon a sloping green
Gay laughing bands of playful boys were are seen
Soon books aloud is thundered from the door
And balls and hoops must harm the hours no more.
But frequent tears the blotted leaves assail
And sighs for dear loved liberty prevail.
Hither by long yet fond remembrance led
With awe we entered the sequestered shed
All eyes are turned the strangers to survey
One tap is hear and all the hint obey
Then grave and courteous rising from his seat
The decent master bows with weakness meet
Invites to sit, looks round with watchful eyes
And bids by signs alternate classes use
Hears, reads, instructs, with solemn voice and allow
Deep busy silence muffling all below.
Dear to the muse to truth, to science dear
Be he who humbly toils and teaches here
His worth his labor shall not sleep forgot
And thus the muse records them as she ought
Of all professions that this world has known
From clowns and cobblers upward to the throne
From the grave architect of Greece and Rome
Down to the framer of a farthing broom
The worst for care and underserved abuse
The first in real dignity and use
If skilled to teach and diligent to rule
Is the learned master if a little school
Not he who guides the legs or skills the clown
To square his fist and knock his fellow down
Not he who shows the still more barbarous art
To parry, thrust, and pierce the unguarded heart
But that good man who, faithful to his charge
Still toils the opening season to enlarge
And leads the growing mind through every stage
From humble, A, B, C, to God’s own page
From numberation through awakening way
Still dark enmities seem clear as day
Pours over the mind a flood of mental light
Expands its wings and gives it powers for flight
Till earth’s remotest bounds and Heaven’s bright train
We trace weight, measure, picture and explain
If such his toil sure honor and regard
And wealth and fame will be his dear reward
Sure every tongue will utter forth his praise
And blessing gild the evening of his days
Yes, blessed indeed with cold ungrateful scorn
With study pale by daily crosses worn
Despised by those who to his labor own
All that they read and almost all the know
Condemned each tedious day such cares to bear
As well might drive even patience to despair
The partial parents taunt the idler dull
The blockheads dark impenetrable skull
The endless round of A, B, C, whole train
Repeated over ten thousand times in vain
Placed an a point the object of each sneer
His faults enlarge, his merits disappear
If mild, "our lazy master loves his ease
The boys at school do anything they please"
If rigid "he’s a cross, hard-hearted wretch
He drives the children stupid with his birch
My child with gentle means will mind a breath
But frowns and floggings frighten him to death"
Do as he will his conduct is arraigned
And dear the little that he gets is gained
Even that he is given him on the quarter day
With looks that sall it money thrown away
Just! Heavens: who knows the unremitting care
And deep solicitude that teachers share
If such their fate by thy divine control
Oh, give them health and fortitude of Soul.
